source.title: A Pre-Training Analogue of Grokking in Language Models: Tracing Delayed Grammatical Generalization
source.authors: Sherin Muckatira; Namrata Shivagunde; Vijeta Deshpande; Anna Rumshisky

record.tranche_reason: Tests grokking-like delayed generalization during natural-language-model pre-training, using BLiMP grammatical evaluation and an exposure-based proxy split rather than the original small algorithmic supervised setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports exposure-conditioned accuracy lags, comparison with matched random splits, and checkpoint-level measures of grammatical representations and attention. No results are recorded for cited studies. The main behavioral result concerns verbatim critical-phrase exposure, not whether the grammar itself was wholly unseen.
record.test_reason: The study trains 35M/60M/130M LLaMA-style models on C4 and measures whether BLiMP examples without verbatim critical-phrase exposure reach 80% accuracy later than exposed examples. It checks this against matched random splits. That is a direct result on grokking-like delay during realistic LM pre-training (V4) on non-algorithmic text (V3, data part only). Its code-length, margin and concept-vector tracking bears weakly on V2's progress-measure part.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that an exposure-based proxy split reveals a pre-training analogue of grokking: exposed BLiMP examples reach 80% accuracy before unexposed ones, beyond what matched random splits produce. They stress it is a checkpoint-level lag, unlike the prolonged many-epoch gap of classical grokking. They also report that most code-length reduction falls in the delay window, that concept vectors become more separable and higher-rank, and that attention-to-context increases in a few heads.
record.recipe_differences: Uses next-token pre-training on C4 and BLiMP examples split by exact critical-phrase exposure; evaluates checkpoint-level accuracy and associated representation/attention measures rather than training small networks on fixed supervised algorithmic datasets.
record.method_sensitivity: The lag varies by grammatical phenomenon, seed, and model size. The 35M model reaches the proxy-validation 80% threshold earlier than the 130M model on most datasets. One eligible dataset, Determiner–Noun Agreement 2, has zero lag in all three seeds; one Regular Subject–Verb Agreement 2 seed does not reach the validation threshold. Results also vary across layers and heads.

fits_no_version.finding: Grammatical concept vectors occupy a higher effective-rank subspace after tafter than at step 100, and attention-to-context increases in a few phenomenon-specific heads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Delayed generalization during LM pre-training is accompanied by increased dimensionality of task-specific concept vectors and localized attention reorganization.

record.problems: The proxy split identifies exact critical-phrase exposure, not whether the grammatical rule was previously unseen. The analysis is limited to five selected phenomena and early checkpoints; the paper retains datasets using a significance-based lag-validation step. The main 60M analyses use three seeds, scale results are shown as curves, and the paper describes checkpoint transition times as estimates because checkpoints are saved every 100 steps.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix Table 8's individual checkpoint-by-checkpoint continuous-margin entries, the full per-layer and per-head attention changes in Appendix Table 10, all-layer results in Appendix Figures 8–10, and attention-entropy curves are not separately tabulated here; the aggregate or selected-head findings directly relevant to V2 are included in r29-r41. Figure-level curves are recorded only where the text gives a corresponding qualitative description.

untested.parts: All of it: small algorithmic datasets, saturated training accuracy with chance test accuracy, and delay versus training-set size.
Identification of a generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, and causal tests.
Switching the delay via initialization scale or weight norm (lazy-to-rich), and images or molecules.
Models above 130M, training beyond the first 2000 steps, and fine-tuning.

missing.what: Numeric log-likelihood margins and accuracies per checkpoint (steps 100–600 and 2000) for each phenomenon, plus C4 training loss
Proxy-validation transition step at thresholds 70–90%, showing that the lag depends on the threshold choice
35M model reaches the validation 80% threshold earlier than the 130M model on most datasets
Selection funnel: 19 datasets generalize too early, 27 never reach 80%, and 4 have proxy-validation that never converges

record.verdict_notes: The proxy-validation split means no verbatim critical-phrase exposure, not unseen grammar. Training accuracy never saturates, and validation does not start at chance for all phenomena. Analyses use only the first 2000 steps, and the five phenomena were retained partly because their lag was significant. I removed the record's V3 limits_scope label with empty rows; the init-scale and weight-norm parts are listed as untested instead.

versions.untested_parts: Small algorithmic datasets, perfect training accuracy alongside chance test accuracy, and how delay changes with training-set size.
Does not identify or causally test a complete generalizing circuit, show removal of memorizing components, or establish that continuous measures anticipate the behavioral transition.
Tests text pre-training only; does not vary initialization scale or weight norm, test a lazy-to-rich transition, or study images or molecules.
Uses models of 35M, 60M, and 130M parameters and early pre-training; does not test frontier-scale models, later pre-training, or fine-tuning.
Weight decay or other low-norm bias, circuit efficiency, critical dataset size, and ungrokking.
Whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm across architectures or hyperparameters.
Adaptive-optimizer instabilities, softmax floating-point limits, and controls for numerical artifacts.

rows.operation_detail: Tracked code length of grammatical proxy-validation critical phrases across checkpoints.
rows.measure: Code length in bits
rows.value: Figure only; text reports substantial code-length reduction during the delayed-generalization window for most phenomena and little reduction later.
rows.note: This is a continuous measure that changes during the transition, but the text does not report that it anticipates the jump.
rows.check: Code length falls during the window before proxy-validation crosses 80%, but validation accuracy is also rising then. There is no sharp jump, so 'anticipation' is weakly shown. The figure has no numbers.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V2. Code length decreases substantially during the delayed-generalization window and changes little afterward; identified circuit formation, memorizing-component removal, and anticipation of the behavioral transition are not established.
source_check.problem: Contemporaneous compression does not establish an incomplete instance of V2's anticipatory circuit mechanism.
